title: Retention Triad: Executive Escalation & Containment Workbook
summary: A lightweight, tactical workbook for rapid assessment and executive escalation when renewal risk crosses critical thresholds. Designed for CS managers to triage, contain, and convert at-risk accounts during the QBR cadence or ad-hoc interventions.
purpose: Provide a single-page operational protocol that blends quantitative signal thresholds with pre-approved containment plays and clear executive handoffs. Reduce time-to-deploy for save plays and make escalation outcomes predictable.
scope: Applies to enterprise and mid-market customers with ARR >= $25k and renewal window within 6 months. Excludes legal/contract disputes that require legal team ownership. Operates alongside standard CSM workflows and QBRs.
triggers: Monthly usage down >40% vs trailing 3-month average
NPS or CSAT drop below 6 on two consecutive surveys
Critical production incident in last 30 days with no remediation plan
Missed SLA(s) with unresolved RCA for >10 business days
Commercial signals: delayed purchase orders, PO changes, or finance disputes
risk_score_matrix: Score each account across Usage (0-5), Health (0-5), Exec Engagement (0-5), Financial Signal (0-5). Total 0-20. 0-7 = Low, 8-13 = Medium, 14-20 = High. High risk requires immediate containment and exec escalation within 48 hours.
escalation_path: Step 1: CSM performs initial triage and updates workbook (within 8 hours)
Step 2: CSM proposes containment play and sets 48-hour standup with Solutions Eng and Support
Step 3: If risk score >= 14, CSM alerts CS Manager and schedules Exec Brief for account owner (within 24 hours)
Step 4: CS Manager + Head of Customer Success decide on executive sponsor engagement and commercial concessions
Step 5: Legal/Finance looped if contract or PO issues present; Sales/AE engaged for commercial remedies
roles_and_responsibilities: CSM: primary owner for day-to-day triage, stakeholder comms, and play execution
CS Manager: approves containment plays, owns exec escalation decisions and cross-functional coordination
Solutions Engineering: rapid technical remediation and POC support for product-related issues
Support/SRE: expedite incident resolution and provide runbook for production issues
AE/Commercial Lead: commercial offers, PO negotiation, and renewal decisioning
Legal/Finance: review and approve any contract or billing changes
immediate_actions: Lock a 48-hour remediation plan with daily checkpoints
Re-establish executive contact top-of-funnel and confirm stakes
Provide a single-page issue brief to customer and internal execs
Apply temporary product guardrails (rate limits, feature toggles) to stabilize environment
Offer a short-term concession tied to measurable remediation milestones
containment_play_templates: Technical Stabilize: Rapid Incident Sprint (24-72 hrs) led by SRE + SE, daily status to execs
Adoption Surge: Targeted enablement sessions for power users + 30-day success pledge
Commercial Stretch: Short-term credits or pilot discount with timeboxed SLA bump
Feature Dialback: Rollback to known-good model or configuration with rollback checklist
Value Re-alignment: Customer workshop to re-scope success metrics and immediate wins
30-60-90_plan: 0-30 days: Stabilize (contain incidents, clear blockers, restore usage signals)
31-60 days: Rebuild confidence (enablement, targeted value delivery, measurable success events)
61-90 days: Cement renewal (executive alignment, contract cadence, prepare final QBR with recovery metrics)
qbr_checklist: Update renewal workbook and score before QBR
Share 1-page status with customer 48 hours before QBR
Include technical owner and commercial owner in QBR invite
Agree on 3 measurable success milestones and owners
Capture commitment language for renewal conversation and next steps
communication_snippets: Exec outreach subject: Quick alignment call on [Customer] renewal and recent incidents
Customer facing one-pager intro: "Your recovery plan at a glance - 3 commitments, owners, timelines"
Internal standup note: "Risk score X -> activation of Retention Triad workbook. Standup 11:00 PST daily."
metrics_to_track: Feature adoption rate for targeted modules
Renewal likelihood change measured in QBR (qualitative)
success_criteria: Usage recovers to within 85% of trailing baseline within 45 days
Zero Sev1 incidents for 30 consecutive days post-stabilization
Executive sponsor confirms renewed commitment by 60 days
Commercial renewal or agreed extension signed within the renewal window
retrospective_questions: What signal(s) did we miss or underweight in the triage?
Was the escalation path executed within target SLAs? If not, why?
Which containment plays were effective and which were not?
Were cross-functional handoffs clear and timely?
What permanent changes should be made to prevent recurrence?
notes_and_tips: Favor measurable, timeboxed concessions over open-ended discounts
Always include a time-limited executive check-in on the calendar (don't leave it as TBD)
Document every customer commitment in the workbook and mirror in email
Use the linked dashboard to ingest signal changes rather than relying on single anecdote
